chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Should we invite the people to this matter? So he said: No, O Fuzayl! Verily, when God intends good for a servant, He commands an angel who seizes him by his neck and enters him into this matter, willingly or unwillingly.

key_terms.الْأَمْر: The matter/cause — a common Shia term referring to the Imamate and Wilayah
key_terms.طَائِعاً أَوْ كَارِهاً: Willingly or unwillingly — emphasizing that divine guidance is irresistible
key_terms.مَلَك: Angel — the divine instrument of guidance in this hadith

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Sadiq say we should invite people to follow the Imams?
ai.summary: Fuzayl ibn Yasar asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) whether he and others should actively invite people to the matter of Wilayah (the guardianship and authority of the Imams). The Imam replied in the negative, explaining that divine guidance is entirely in God's hands: when God wills goodness for a person, He commands an angel to bring that person into this path regardless of their initial disposition. This hadith teaches that true guidance (hidayah) is a divine act, not the product of human missionary effort, and reflects the Shia theological understanding of divine will in spiritual matters.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Should we be inviting the people to this matter (Al-Wilayah)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, O Fuzayl! Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, when He<sup>azwj</sup> Intends good with a servant, Commands an Angel. So he seizes him by his neck and enters him into this matter, willingly or unwillingly’.
